concept.title: MCP Server Integration
concept.shortdesc: DitaCraft exposes its DITA intelligence — validation, key space resolution, context snapshots, and map analysis — to external AI agents via the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

section.title: Overview
section.p: The MCP server lets AI coding agents like opencode, Claude Desktop, Cursor, and Continue read and query your DITA workspace. It runs as a standalone Node.js process with no VS Code dependency — agents spawn it directly via stdio.
The server exposes 6 tools and 3 resources:

strow.stentry: Validate a DITA file or XML fragment and return diagnostics with error counts and severity
Token-budgeted map snapshot for LLM prompt injection (Levels 1/2/3)
List all defined keys and their resolved targets with scope and provenance filters
Return map topic hierarchy as JSON, tree text, or CSV
Resolve href, keyref, conref, or conkeyref to target file and element
Step-by-step key resolution trace with scope and keyref chain details

section.title: Building the MCP Server
section.p: Run the standalone build command from the DitaCraft project root:
section.codeblock: npm run build-standalone # → dist/mcp-server.js (3.2 MB) # → dist/lsp-server.js (2.0 MB)
section.p: Both bundles are self-contained — no node_modules needed at runtime.

section.title: Standalone LSP Server
section.p: DitaCraft also ships a standalone LSP server bundle for embedding in other Node.js projects:
Set the DITACRAFT_EXTENSION_ROOT environment variable to point to the directory containing the dtds/ folder. The LSP server uses stdin/stdout for JSON-RPC communication.

section.title: Workspace Security
section.p: The MCP server enforces workspace isolation:

ul.li: All file paths are resolved relative to the WORKSPACE environment variable
Path traversal attacks (../../ beyond 8 levels) are rejected
HTTP URLs, UNC paths, and null bytes are rejected
No document content is ever transmitted to external services

section.note: The MCP server uses stdio transport by default, which means all communication stays local to the machine. No network configuration is required.
